predecessors.name: Sultanate of Rum
predecessors.text: the region round Balıkesir, which the Karasids 'are thought to have taken over ... during the reign of Mesud II'

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Balıkesir, Bergama (Pergamon) and Edremit, the lands Dursun 'offered' to Orhan, taken in 1345

ledger.x: 1296: Karasi Bey founds the Karasid beylik round Balıkesir.
1302: the Byzantine campaign in western Anatolia with the Catalan Company and the Alans opens the fighting in the region; Karasi's expansion into Lesser Mysia follows it (undated).
1308: the Byzantine campaign of 1302-1308 ends; the page puts Karasi's expansion into Lesser Mysia after it, with no year (1308 is the earliest).
1308 at the earliest: Karasi holds Lesser Mysia.

wars.name: Karasid expansion into Lesser Mysia
wars.outcome: 'Following the Byzantine campaign in western Anatolia allied with Catalan Company and Alans between 1302 and 1308, Karasi expanded into Lesser Mysia' (Karasids page: the expansion follows the 1302-1308 campaign, so 1308 is its earliest year, not a dated span…

wars.name: Treaty of Pegai between Andronikos III and the Karasids
wars.outcome: Andronikos III 'met with Demir Khan in Pegai in 1328, when they signed a treaty'; the page does not give its terms.

wars.name: Ottoman annexation of Karasi
wars.outcome: Orhan, as 'a bringer of peace' between two rival claimants, pushes the brothers into the castle at Pergamum (one killed, one captured) and takes the Karasid lands in 1345.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary; the frontiers with the Byzantines, Germiyan and Saruhan are approximate throughout.
